subject: Pricing follow-up: target $/1M token benchmarking - Redwood vs OpenAI/Anthropic
messages:
From: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.com>
To: Alex Johnson <alex.johnson@acme.com>
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.com, rishi_malhotra@redwood.com
Date: Fri, 12 Mar 2027 15:02:00 -0700
Subject: Follow-up + benchmarking: target $/1M tokens (Redwood vs OpenAI/Anthropic)

Alex — great to meet today, thanks for taking the time. Quick recap and next steps from our discovery: 

Call recap:
- Primary use: customer support summarization + follow-up generation for ~4M monthly messages (mix of short/long).
- Expected average prompt + response length: ~1.5k tokens per request on peak workflows (~40% of requests), long-form summaries ~8k tokens for batch jobs (~10% of requests).
- Estimated monthly token volume (initial): 150M	300M tokens (growing to ~1B over 12 months if pilot successful).
- Key procurement constraint: target cost on hosted inference ideally <= $300–400 per 1M tokens to fit unit economics.

What we heard on budget and goals:
- You indicated a target $/1M tokens of roughly $300 as a stretch target and $450 as acceptable.
- High priority: predictable unit cost as volume scales.
- Secondary: model quality parity with OpenAI/Anthropic for instruction-following on customer conversations.

Attached I included: Redwood_pricing_comparison_v1.pdf (high-level $/1M benchmarking), Token_benchmark_sheet.xlsx (your volumes mapped to cost tiers), and a draft SOW outline.

High-level benchmarking (quick summary):
- OpenAI (gpt-4o family) public list pricing example: ~$900–1200 / 1M tokens for top-tier models (varies by contract).
- Anthropic (Claude advanced) example: ~$700–1000 / 1M tokens depending on package.
- Open-model hosts (self-hosted / managed): ranges widely — $150–600 / 1M tokens depending on quantization, batch sizing, and reserved capacity.
- Redwood typical target for enterprise committed customers (with reserved/dedicated capacity + quantization guidance): $250–450 / 1M tokens at scale, depending on model selection and caching.

Questions / next steps:
1) Can you confirm the monthly token range you'd be comfortable starting the pilot with (choose a bracket: 150–300M, 300–600M, 600M+)?
2) Any procurement guardrails we should know (PO process length, legal redlines on data residency)?
3) Would you like a follow-up with our Performance PM to map observed token mix to expected per-token cost (we typically run a short benchmark using your sample traces)?

I can put together a two-tier price proposal (pilot pricing + committed reserved pricing) that shows: target $/1M, expected unit economics at your modeled volumes, and comparison versus OpenAI/Anthropic. If it helps, we can target the pilot proposal around your $300/1M stretch target and show what reserve/commit level would be needed to hit that.

Thanks — I’ll hold off on formal pricing until you confirm the starting volume bracket.

Best,
Vanessa Ortiz
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
vanessa_ortiz@redwood.com | +1 (415) 555-0172
Redwood Inference

---
Attachments: Redwood_pricing_comparison_v1.pdf (summary), Token_benchmark_sheet.xlsx (volume mapping)
From: Alex Johnson <alex.johnson@acme.com>
To: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.com>
Cc: procurement@acme.com
Date: Mon, 15 Mar 2027 09:14:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Follow-up + benchmarking: target $/1M tokens (Redwood vs OpenAI/Anthropic)

Thanks Vanessa — good call. Quick answers inline:

- Starting bracket: 150–300M tokens/month for the pilot (we expect to ramp to ~700–900M within 9–12 months if all goes well).
- Procurement: standard PO + 60-day net payment; legal will push on data residency and audit rights (we need SOC2 and a data flow diagram).
- Yes, please do a short benchmark using a representative sample trace (I can share example logs) — would like to see per-token delta between Redwood-managed infra vs our current Anthropic/hosted provider.

On pricing: your summary looks promising. To be explicit — our internal target for unit economics is $300 / 1M tokens or lower for core support flows. For experimental/long-form batch jobs we can tolerate up to $600/1M. If you can show a committed reserved price that hits $300 / 1M at ~600M committed monthly, that will be compelling.

Can you also include assumed latency SLOs and the quantization approach in the benchmark? That matters for quality comparisons.

Appreciate it — Alex
Alex Johnson
Head of Automation, Acme Corp
alex.johnson@acme.com | +1 (212) 555-0199
From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: vanessa_ortiz@redwood.com, rishi_malhotra@redwood.com
Date: Mon, 15 Mar 2027 09:37:00 -0700
Subject: Re: internal: pricing buckets to propose for ACME

Vanessa / Rishi — internal note with suggested pricing buckets (draft):

Assumptions: pilot volume 150–300M; committed volume tiering at 300M, 600M, 1B+. Use dedicated GPU reservation for predictability + mixed-precision quantized models for cost.

Suggested public-facing tiers (round numbers):
- Pilot (no commit, 150–300M): $550 / 1M tokens (hosted, reserved burst, includes support + 30-day onboarding credit)
- Committed Tier 300M/month: $420 / 1M tokens (12mo commitment, standard SLAs)
- Committed Tier 600M/month: $320 / 1M tokens (12mo commitment + 10% volume smoothing allowance)
- Committed Tier 1B+/month: $240 / 1M tokens (enterprise negotiation, dedicated pool + SRE oncall)

Rationale: these reflect current observed unit economics vs open-model hosts after quantization/batching gains and include our margin + commercial support. Hitting $300/1M requires ~600M committed with reserved capacity and a small add-on for performance tuning.

Attachments: I updated Token_benchmark_sheet.xlsx with sample cost calc and target lines. Recommend offering a 6-8 week performance benchmark with a clear ingress sample to validate quality vs Anthropic.

If you want to push hard on the $300/1M stretch for the pilot, we could offer a time-limited pilot discount to $420/1M for 3 months but require a 6mo commit to extend. Thoughts?

- Marissa (Sales Ops)
From: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.com>
To: Alex Johnson <alex.johnson@acme.com>
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.com, rishi_malhotra@redwood.com, procurement@acme.com
Date: Mon, 15 Mar 2027 09:40:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Follow-up + benchmarking: target $/1M tokens (Redwood vs OpenAI/Anthropic)

Alex — thanks for the confirmation and the clarity on targets. Next steps and what I’m sending you now:

1) Attached: Redwood_pricing_comparison_v1.pdf (updated) + Token_benchmark_sheet.xlsx (updated with your pilot bracket and the suggested committed tiers). Key lines:
   - Pilot (150–300M): $550 / 1M tokens (no commit)
   - Committed 300M/mo: $420 / 1M tokens
   - Committed 600M/mo: $320 / 1M tokens -> this is where we can hit your $300 goal with a small extra tuning/discount as discussed internally
   - Committed 1B+/mo: $240 / 1M tokens (enterprise negotiation)

2) Benchmark: Rishi (cc’d) will run a quality + performance benchmark using your sample traces. We’ll include latency SLOs (p95 generation latency targets per token class) and quantization notes in the deliverable. Please share the sample traces (anonymized) via the Drive link or secure upload.

3) Procurement / SOC2: I attached a SOC2 factsheet and our standard data flow diagram. Legal/procurement, feel free to flag any specific redlines — we’ll surface those to our Contracts team.

If you’re okay, I’ll schedule a 30-min follow-up next Wednesday to walk the benchmark plan and pricing tiers with your engineering and procurement teams.

Thanks — looking forward to getting the benchmark running.

Best,
Vanessa Ortiz
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
vanessa_ortiz@redwood.com | +1 (415) 555-0172
